critical.issue: Required private cache header contract is not preserved on public endpoint responses. Observed Cache-Control='no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate' (missing 'private') while local backend direct port 8001 correctly returns 'no-store, private'.

action_items: Fix edge/public response header policy so private document endpoints keep `Cache-Control: no-store, private` exactly (currently rewritten upstream).
After header fix, rerun backend privacy assertions for assets, metadata list, and PDF download endpoints through public domain (not localhost).
critical_code_review_comments: Content ID privacy headers are set correctly in app code (contentid_assets.PRIVATE_HEADERS), but public ingress/edge response rewriting drops the `private` directive; this is a deployment-layer security/compliance gap for private documents.

Validation coverage is strong: duplicate NIK rejection, swapped signature/KTP asset rejection, foreign/malformed image rejection, oversize enforcement (5MB signature / 10MB KTP), and in-progress idempotency 409 all behaved as expected.
Direct `/api/files/contentid-private/...` (including normalized alias `./`) is correctly blocked with 404 on public URL.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend pytest file is ready for regression: /app/backend/tests/test_iter68_content_id_claim.py. Public-vs-local header discrepancy was reproduced deterministically: public domain returns `no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate` while direct backend 8001 returns `no-store, private` for same asset endpoint and token. Local PDF artifact and rendered pages are preserved under /app/test_reports for visual/legal text inspection; source R2 objects for the UI-created ticket were cleaned.
rca of the issue: RCA: The backend code sends PRIVATE_HEADERS including `Cache-Control: no-store, private`, but responses through public preview domain lose `private` and become `no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate`. Reproduction: (1) login label fixture, (2) fetch bound asset and ticket document metadata via public `/api/tickets/content-id/...`, (3) observe header mismatch; (4) repeat same request directly against `http://127.0.0.1:8001/api/...` with same bearer token and see correct `no-store, private`. This indicates upstream/ingress cache header rewrite, not route handler logic.
